messages:
Alex: heads-up — acme reported a sharp p95/p99 latency increase starting ~03:10 UTC, p99 ~6s now, previously ~1.2s. They see a bunch of 504s.
Maya: thanks. do we have tenant id / request ids? any recent deploys?
Alex: tenant: acme-inc (tenant_id=acme_42). example req: rQeST-9a3. No infra deploys on their cluster, but there was a config rollout for admission-window earlier today.
Sam: pulling metrics now — querying per-tenant queue length + worker saturation. run: curl -s "http://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=redwood_ingress_queue_length{tenant=\"acme_42\"}" | jq .
Sam: results: queue_length spiked from ~5 to ~480 at 03:09, inflight concurrency saturated at 128 (our limit). p95 token latency follows queue length.
Jordan: oncall note — admission controller logs show repeated "admit_rejected: concurrency_limit" for acme_42. looks like the admission window size was lowered in the canary (rolled at 02:50).
Maya: ok that matches — we changed default admit_window_ms for cpu-backed workers from 200 -> 40 in the latest perf tweak for smaller models. unintended side-effect: long-tail requests now pile up.
Sam: mitigation options: 1) bump admit window back for tenant, 2) increase tenant concurrency (hotfix), 3) route acme to the fallback pool (larger concurrency), 4) enable short-term prefix-KV caching for their workloads. quickest: bump admit window or increase concurrency.
Alex: customer is seeing timeouts, asking for ETA. recommended immediate action?
Jordan: emergency patch to config map: kubectl -n redwood apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-admit-config
data:
  acme_42.admit_window_ms: "200"
  acme_42.max_concurrency: "256"
EOF
Jordan: I'll run that for acme now (one-off override).
Maya: also rolling back the global change from 200->40 is safer long-term. I'll queue a rollback and add a canary guard to avoid per-tenant blowups.
deploy-bot: deploy started for config patch (patch-id: cfg-2026-0317-01) :gear:
Sam: after patch: queue_length dropped to ~8 within 30s, p99 back to ~1.4s. no further 504s reported in logs.
Alex: updating the customer: "We've applied a tenant-level admit/concurrency override that reduced queueing — monitoring shows tail latency returning to normal. We'll follow up with a formal RCA and a rollout rollback."
Nina: please collect repro steps + perf comparison for RCA: before (admit_window_ms=40) vs after (200) for a representative load. we need numbers for the postmortem.
Maya: repro steps I used: run loadgen with per-tenant arrival distribution to match their 95th percentile sequence lengths: 
```
# quick repro (local loadgen)
PYTHONPATH=. python tools/loadgen.py --tenant acme_42 --rps 1200 --concurrency 200 --seq-dist longtail --duration 5m
```
Collect: redwood_ingress_queue_length, ingress_inflight_concurrency, per-token latency histogram.
Sam: logs/commands to fetch slices: 
```
# sample logs for tenant
kubectl logs -l app=ingress --tail=500 | grep acme_42 | sed -n '1,200p'
# metrics snapshot
curl -s "http://metrics.internal/api/v1/query_range?query=redwood_ingress_queue_length{tenant=\"acme_42\"}&start=$(date -d '5 minutes ago' +%s)&end=$(date +%s)&step=10"
```
Jordan: note for RCA: check admission controller's histogram buckets — the 40ms window reduced batching opportunities, increasing CPU per-request due to less batching and producing more schedule churn.
Maya: long-term: we'll add a canary rule that prevents admit_window changes from getting applied to tenants with sustained concurrency > X, and add automated smoke for p95 regression after config rollouts.
Alex: customer updated and happy with temporary fix, wants ETA for permanent fix. I'll sync with acme CS and schedule follow-up.
Nina: we'll own the RCA + timeline. Maya/Sam/Jordan please attach metrics + logs to the ticket. thanks. :thumbsup:
